persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Anthropic's S-1 shaped Bora Özkent's day: he finds the document "better than expected" because Q2 2026 shows a first-ever operating profit of $974 million, revenue per employee of $6.6 million second only to **Nvidia**, and $3.929 billion of operating cash inflow. He sees most of the $80 billion net loss as a valuation charge; on the other hand the non-cancellable compute commitments of $161 billion to **Broadcom**, $120 billion to **SpaceX** and $114 billion to **Google** would be a heavy burden if growth slows. He will not decide before the price is known, but is thinking of entering with a small position so that "his foot is in"; on the news, index futures are up about 1.5% and **SMH** 3.12%.

In his weekly video he says that with the US, Israeli and Brazilian elections, the Fed and PCE, and mega-cap earnings all landing in the same week he expects little good from markets, sees a poor technical picture and says new pullbacks may come. Even so, the S&P 500 forward P/E has fallen from 22.2 at the start of the year to 18.8, while most earnings growth comes from **Nvidia** and **Micron**. He reads **Meta**'s plan to sell up to $95 billion of stock as a sign that the AI infrastructure race needs more financing and that chip demand will continue. On the election side, he notes that a Netanyahu loss could bring Middle East peace pricing, and that after midterms the S&P 500 has historically risen.

items.title: Anthropic's Earnings Are Better Than I Expected.
items.summary: Bora Özkent finds Anthropic's S-1 better than expected: about $11.5 billion revenue in the last quarter (up 1368%), revenue per employee of $6.6 million (behind only Nvidia's $7.21 million; a year ago $1.4 million) and $112.4 billion cash plus $19.3 billion short-term investments. In Q2 2026 there is a first-ever operating profit of $974 million and net operating cash inflow of $3.929 billion in the first 6 months. Of the $80 billion net loss, $72.4 billion is the revaluation of debt convertible into shares and about $8 billion is the cost of deals with Google and Amazon. There are 11,900 customers spending over $100K, 1,900 over $1M and about 250 over $10M; net revenue retention is 900% and the top five customers' share of revenue fell from 36% to 21%. Risks: largely non-cancellable compute commitments of $161 billion to Broadcom, $120 billion to SpaceX and $114 billion to Google, over 80% of revenue coming from the last 6 months' models, share dilution, and a last-round valuation of about $1 trillion against market expectations of $1.5-2 trillion. Bora will decide once the price is known but wants a small position to be in; the market liked the news, with index futures up 1.5% and SMH up 3.12%. He expects the October revenue to be leaked before the IPO.

assets.note: Financials are better than expected; he considers a small position once the price is known, but flags competition and dilution risks.
Anthropic has a ~$161B compute commitment to Broadcom.

items.title: The Hardest Week for Markets!
items.summary: Bora Özkent describes this week as the busiest he can remember, with the US, Israeli and Brazilian elections, the Fed decision, PCE, jobs data and mega-cap tech earnings all overlapping. Last week the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell; his own semiconductor-heavy portfolio is up 24% year to date but off a peak near 45%. The S&P 500 forward P/E has fallen from 22.2 in January to 18.8, and 34% of the rise in Q3 earnings expectations comes from Nvidia and Micron. The unwinding of leveraged funds exaggerated the moves and may be close to its end. Musk is attacking neocloud companies, SpaceX arranged $40 billion of debt and chip-collateralized debt has reached a trillion dollars; Apple briefly passed Nvidia because it does not spend on AI. On Thursday PCE is expected to rise from 3% to 3.1% core and from 3.4% to 3.6% headline, and Bora expects no surprise from PCE or the Fed. In the midterms Democrats are expected to take the House; turbulence may last until November 3, but from the midterms to June 30 the S&P 500 has risen 15.5% on average since 1950. After Lula's win EWZ fell about 20%; the Israeli election concludes tomorrow and a Netanyahu loss could bring Middle East peace pricing. He expects little good from markets this week and the technical picture is poor.

assets.note: Most of the earnings-expectation rise comes from Nvidia and Micron; Apple briefly passed Nvidia.

In the earnings flow **Celestica**, **Cadence** and **Rambus** beat expectations while **Amkor**, **Nucor** EPS and **Whirlpool** fell short.

persons.name: jrouldz
persons.digest: jrouldz wrote that when AI stocks were at highs everyone was certain of their thesis, that doubt set in once valuations collapsed and that **Musk** is exploiting the fear; he thinks Musk's words should be read as "what he wants us to hear" rather than "what he thinks". He noted that the list of AI buildout companies with revenue outside data centers is short (**AMZN**, **SPCX**, **META**, **GOOG**, **MSFT**, **ORCL**). Although he sees some relief on charts, he says it is "far too early to call a reversal".

items.title: Psychology in AI stocks

persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest: cevikfinance argues that Musk's statement is not a disaster for neocloud companies but a supply constraint that will keep GPU rental prices high for those with power infrastructure in place, and counts the fact that companies such as **Nebius** did not crash on Monday as confirmation. He wrote that **Celestica** again reported a very strong quarter and that he loves the company.

items.title: Neoclouds did not crash on Musk's statement
items.summary: cevikfinance wrote that everyone expected neoclouds to crash but they did not, and that Musk's statement is positive for neoclouds with power infrastructure ready.

assets.note: A supply constraint keeping GPU rental prices high for power-ready neoclouds, positive.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies

mentions.quote: SoFi is where finance meets technology. An investment that has upset its investors.
07:00: SoFi (SOFI)

holdings.why: wallstengine's calendar shows earnings today at 07:00 ET; Bora Özkent calls it "an investment that has upset its investors" but gives no clear buy or sell rationale.
holdings.opinion: It is the largest holding (18.8%) and earnings are today; results and guidance could drive the position's move in a single day. The main risk is that one stock is about a fifth of the portfolio.
ai_points: Against: One stock is about a fifth of the portfolio, so earnings-day volatility risk is high.
For: The sources give no concrete signal to cut the position ahead of earnings.
Against: Bora Özkent calls the stock an investment that has upset its investors.

holdings.name: Amundi MSCI Turkey (Acc)

mentions.quote: If you look at the details BlackRock exited the stocks in May-June. That is, around 14500.

holdings.why: According to ulkser BlackRock's Turkey exit happened in May-June around 14,500 and is not a current flight; Tunç Şatıroğlu says the FX policy carries devaluation risk after the election.
holdings.opinion: Because the Turkey index is held in euro terms, lira weakness can directly erode returns; the balance between local equity gains and currency loss is what to watch.
ai_points: For: According to ulkser the foreign exit news is old, with no current selling pressure.
Against: According to Tunç Şatıroğlu, FX suppression could bring a bigger devaluation after the election.
Against: A euro-based position is exposed to lira weakness.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: This is the main reason I have long followed Broadcom alongside NVIDIA.
Broadcom organized a $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic's AI chips.

holdings.why: FinancewithIzzy highlights the $115B AI revenue target for 2027 and korkmazali08 relays the $63B financing structure for Anthropic; neither gives a new level or date.
holdings.opinion: The ~$161B Broadcom compute commitment in Anthropic's S-1 improves demand visibility but adds dependence on the success of Anthropic's IPO and the financing structure.
ai_points: For: According to Bora Özkent, Anthropic has a $161B compute commitment to Broadcom.
For: According to FinancewithIzzy, AI revenue targets are ~$58B in 2026 and $115B in 2027.
Against: Broadcom guarantees part of the chips' future value, which means taking on risk.

holdings.name: Meta Platforms A

mentions.quote: Meta's AI products are lifting ad revenue, but spending growth is for now faster than cash generation.
Meta aims to sell up to $95 billion in stock to fund its AI spending.
$META announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two offerings.

holdings.why: According to korkmazali08 capex is $34.9B and free cash flow -$2.12B; the $35B equity offering brings dilution but the sources give no concrete level to sell.
holdings.opinion: Revenue growth is strong (26%) but capex outpaces cash generation and the share issuance dilutes; 12.8% of the portfolio rides on this thesis, and what matters is when AI revenue covers capex.
ai_points: For: According to korkmazali08, Q3 revenue rose 26% and Q4 is guided to $73-76B.
Against: Free cash flow is -$2.12B and 2026 capex is $135-145B.
Against: The $35B offering and $60B ATM program bring dilution.

Against: High-beta stocks fall harder when risk appetite weakens.
Against: The sources contain no concrete information on this holding.

Against: Growth stocks can fall together if market-wide risk appetite weakens.
Against: The sources contain no concrete information on this holding.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: The tone at the press conference could determine the direction of the 10-year yield at the 5% line.

holdings.why: According to WallStDiaries the Fed's tone on Wednesday could set the direction of the 10-year yield at the 5% line; Bora Özkent expects no surprise from the Fed.
holdings.opinion: The long-dated US Treasury fund is highly sensitive to rates; with inflation at 3.7% and a hike possible, higher yields are a direct price risk. It balances AI equities in the portfolio but its duration is long.
ai_points: For: Provides balance to the portfolio during equity selloffs.
Against: According to WallStDiaries inflation is 3.7% and a hike at later meetings is on the table.
Against: According to Bora Özkent, headline PCE inflation is expected to rise from 3.4% to 3.6%.
